# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `unit_no_password_in_argv` against input/. The base case,
# tests/fixtures/doctor/unit_no_password_in_argv/expect.json, carries the _env caveat (DESIGN.md
# §2i freezes no override that points the doctor at a directory of unit FILES -- a gap Phase 0
# records rather than fills), the "how to read this file" convention, and the rule that the node
# unit's own rpc-login= in its --config-file is CORRECT and must not be reported.
# input/ is that case's two units with ONE LINE CHANGED; the changed file says which at its top.
#
# THIS CASE: the wallet unit's ExecStart carries --rpc-login.
# §2c: the wallet unit passes NEITHER --disable-rpc-login NOR --rpc-login, precisely so that
# monero-wallet-rpc generates its own 128-bit credential into WorkingDirectory as
# monero-wallet-rpc.<port>.login, at mode 0400, and deletes it on exit
# (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:351-380; src/common/util.cpp:215-224, :263). fmonero never
# generates, writes or rotates that secret -- it reads it.
# TWO SEPARATE THINGS ARE WRONG HERE, and the second is the one that matters: the two flags are
# mutually exclusive and passing both is fatal (:341-349), but this unit passes only one, so it
# WOULD START. It would simply put a credential in /proc/<pid>/cmdline, which is
# world-readable -- a silent, working, leaking configuration, which is why this is an
# error-severity check and not a startup failure.
# CONTRAST THE NODE UNIT, which is UNCHANGED in this case and is CORRECT: its credential is in
# ~/.config/fmonero/monerod.conf at mode 0600, referenced by --config-file, because monerod
# does NOT auto-generate one (§1b.6). A detector that greps for the string "rpc-login"
# anywhere reports both units and is wrong about one of them.
# THE VALUE IN THE FIXTURE IS THE LITERAL "REDACTED-PLACEHOLDER", NOT A CREDENTIAL (§2b.2).
